When working with a function of two  variables, the closed interval is replaced by a closed, bounded set. A set is bounded if all the points in that set can be  contained within a ball (or disk) of finite radius. First, we need to find the critical points inside the set and calculate the  corresponding critical values. Then, it is necessary to find the maximum and minimum value of the function on the  boundary of the set. When we have all these values, the largest function value corresponds to the global maximum and  the smallest function value corresponds to the absolute minimum.
